interventions.speaker: CHAIR
interventions.who: the senior urologist who signs the decision
interventions.body:
The prognosis is influenced by several documented factors. The surgical findings include a Gleason 3+4 (ISUP grade group 2) and positive surgical margins, which are concerning features. Conversely, the seminal vesicles were not invaded, and lymphovascular invasion was absent. Nodal status is documented as positive lymph node metastasis. The preoperative PSA was 4.1. The biopsy grade (Gleason 3+4) matches the prostatectomy specimen, which is a consistent finding.

The primary countervailing finding is the absence of extraprostatic extension. Missing information that would significantly revise the prognosis includes the postoperative PSA and its subsequent trajectory. The current nodal status and positive margins suggest a higher risk profile. The uncertainty in the prognosis is reflected in the heuristic sensitivity range for recurrence time. Missing postoperative PSA or follow-up data will widen the uncertainty regarding the trajectory of the disease. The fixed estimated horizon is 64.18 months. This represents expected follow-up without an event, not a known recurrence date. The sensitivity range is 51.35–77.02 months; its coverage has not been validated.
